Senator Reed’s outrage over SNAP cuts ignores the core issue: bloated bureaucracy enabling dependency. The Improving Access to Nutrition Act of 2025 (S.1628) repeals work requirements, incentivizing perpetual reliance on taxpayer-funded aid. Section 6(o) removal prioritizes handouts over accountability—exactly why programs balloon beyond $370M/year in RI alone.

Trump’s reforms redirect funds to targeted relief, not open-ended entitlements. Fraudulent claims and administrative waste drain resources; work requirements ensure aid reaches those truly in need while fostering self-sufficiency.

Real reform cuts red tape, not just budgets.
